x: Novices c.c. race, and Eric Bishop was second in the Inter-Banks Junior event. Brian Trower finished third in the Portsmouth A.C. open 5 miles road handicap race, with a start of 3 min. 10 secs., and has also been running with the R.A.F., Sopley.
Finally Eric Bishop motor cycled all the way with his wife, and adquately made up for the very poor support our runners received from the Club generally.

Eric Bishop was 3rd in the mile and George Stace was similarly placed in the 2 miles event with his best performance to date. In the latter race we had Tom Carter in action and although his speed is not of former years his style is as good as ever.
On the day of the Club 7, Cliff Roffey was 4th and David Baulch 7th in the Civil Service Cross Country Championship, whilst Eric Bishop was 16th in the Inter-Banks.
Eric and Alan Bishop who were fourth at the start, moved up to 2nd place having run an extremely well judged race. The positions of the other pairs changed very little throughout the event.

Eddie Short 28th, looked fairly happy and so did Eric and Alan Bishop who were now 32nd and 45th respectively. Between them was Brian Trower who shouted out that he was going to retire, but the reception given to his remark made him decide to finish the course.
Apart from the races on Easter Monday, the only report received is on the Finchley 20 which was held on April 21st and was sent in by Eric Bishop.

Other Club members taking part were, Eric Gebbett 23rd in 2H.42m.56s., Alan Bishop 29th in 2h.51m.7s. and Eric Bishop 36th in 3h.1m.57s. The latter did very well to finish the course as he had only one month's training in preparation for this race, having had achilles tendon trouble since the early part of the year.
